templates.title: The "Site Survey" (Discovery Report)
templates.note: Used in Week 1 to document the "messy reality" before you start building.
templates.code:
### 🕵️ Site Survey: [Client Name] - [Project Name]
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD | **Lead FDE:** [Your Name]

#### 1. The Data Landscape (The Ground Truth)
- **Source Systems:** [e.g., On-prem SQL Server 2016, SAP HANA, Unstructured Sharepoint]
- **Data Gravity:** [e.g., 5TB total, growing at 50GB/day. Must stay within EU regions.]
- **Known Quality Issues:** [e.g., Missing timestamps in 30% of records, no primary keys in CRM.]

#### 2. Technical & Security Constraints
- **Identity:** [e.g., Client uses Okta for OIDC. Need to integrate with GCP IAM.]
- **Connectivity:** [e.g., No public internet. Must use Cloud Interconnect + Private Google Access.]
- **Exfiltration Risks:** VPC Service Controls (VPC SC) are active. Need to request perimeter bridges.

#### 3. The "Delta" (The Gap)
- **Product Gap:** Core product doesn't support the client's proprietary `.xyz` file format.
- **Proposed Glue:** Build a custom GCF (Cloud Function) parser to convert `.xyz` to Parquet.

#### 4. The Quick Win (Week 2 Objective)
- [e.g., Stand up an Agent Search instance on the 'Policy' dataset to prove 90% retrieval accuracy.]

templates.title: The Technical Scoping & PRD
templates.note: The "Contract" that defines what success looks like.
templates.code:
### 📐 Technical Scoping Document: [Feature Name]

#### 1. Objective & User Persona
Enable **[User Group, e.g., Risk Analysts]** to perform **[Action, e.g., Fraud Investigation]** by leveraging **[Technology, e.g., Multi-Agent ADK Swarm]**.

#### 2. Definition of Success (The Evals)
*Success is not "it works"; success is measurable:*
- **Retrieval:** >90% Hit Rate on Top-3 documents.
- **Latency:** End-to-end agent reasoning < 5 seconds.
- **Groundedness:** 0% Hallucination rate on Golden Dataset (manually verified by Client).

#### 3. Phased Deployment Strategy
- **Phase 1 (MVP):** Manual trigger agent on Cloud Run using BigQuery static export.
- **Phase 2 (Scale):** Automated trigger via Pub/Sub on real-time data stream.

#### 4. Out of Scope
- Integration with the legacy AS400 mainframe (deferred to Q3).

templates.title: The Executive Status Report (The "WES")
templates.note: The weekly document that justifies the contract renewal.
templates.code:
## 🛰️ Weekly Executive Summary: [Project Name]
**Reporting Period:** [Date Range] | **Status:** 🟢 GREEN

#### 🚀 Value Delivered This Week
- **Metric Move:** Reduced manual data lookup time for Analysts by **40%** via the new Search Agent.
- **Milestone:** Successfully cleared the Security Review for the GKE Private Cluster.
- **Ingestion:** 1.2B rows of historical logs moved into BigQuery; partitioning optimized for cost.

#### ⚠️ Risks & Strategic Blockers
- **Risk:** Client IT team has delayed the Firewall port opening for the VPN.
- **Impact:** Potential 3-day slide on the "Real-time" dashboard milestone.
- **Action Required:** Need [Executive Sponsor Name] to approve the exception ticket #12345.

#### 🗓️ The "Day 30" Horizon
- Finalize **Pairwise Evaluation** run for the production agent.
- Transition 1st-line support to the internal Client Ops team.

glossary.definition: Pioneered by Palantir, this refers to the "gap" between what a product does out-of-the-box and the specific engineering required to make it solve a client's mission.
The philosophy of solving a client’s unique problem through code that can eventually be abstracted back into the core product features.
Unlike a consultant who "advises," an FDE is embedded—they have client credentials, sit in client Slack channels, and ship code directly into the client’s production environment.
The complex work of stitching a modern SaaS/AI platform into legacy, often undocumented, "messy" enterprise systems.

Environments with zero or intermittent internet connectivity (Common in Defense/Energy). Requires local container registries and offline model weights. See the Air-Gapped & Tactical Edge Deployment section for the full playbook.
A GCP security perimeter that prevents data exfiltration by restricting access to Google-managed services (like BigQuery or Agent Platform) only from authorized networks.
The process of moving a prototype from "it works on my machine" to "it meets SOC2/HIPAA security standards," including encryption at rest/transit and least-privilege IAM roles.
Unauthorized tools or "rogue" databases used by client employees. This is often where the "cleanest" and most useful data actually lives.
The authoritative data source for a given piece of information (e.g., SAP for finance, Salesforce for CRM). FDEs must identify this to avoid building on "stale" data replicas.

glossary.term: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
glossary.definition: Google's umbrella brand (announced at Google Cloud Next '26) for the full agent-building stack — Model Garden, Agent Studio, Agent Runtime, Agent Search, Vector Search, Evals, Model Monitoring, and more. Existing Vertex AI SDKs, APIs (aiplatform.v1beta1.), and billing are unchanged; only the product-level branding and console UI have moved.

glossary.term: Agent Runtime (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine)
glossary.definition: The managed, auto-scaling runtime for deploying agents built with ADK, LangChain, LangGraph, or any Python framework. Sits under "Scale" in the Agent Platform console alongside Memory Bank and Sessions.

Launched in Alpha at Google Cloud Next '26 (April 22, 2026), an opinionated CLI + seven-skill package (google-agents-cli-workflow, -scaffold, -adk-code, -eval, -deploy, -publish, -observability) that turns any AI coding tool (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity) into an ADK-lifecycle expert — and also runs standalone from the terminal. Installed via uvx google-agents-cli setup.
An open standard used in the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) that allows autonomous agents to discover, hand off tasks, and communicate with one another across systems.
Deterministic agents in ADK (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) that follow fixed logic paths rather than relying on an LLM to "plan" the next step.
The process of connecting an LLM to "Ground Truth" data (via RAG or Google Search) to ensure its responses are factual and cite-able.

A GCP-native evaluation method where an "Autorater" LLM compares two model outputs and provides a structured judgment on which is better and why. Runs inside Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Evals (formerly Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service).
A measure of how much the answer is derived only from the retrieved context, essentially a "hallucination score".
The legally binding "fence" around your project. If it’s not in the SOW, it’s "Scope Creep".
The high-level contract between your company and the client that defines the legal relationship before any specific work starts.
A strategic argument used to drive projects forward by quantifying how much money/efficiency the client loses every day they don't deploy the solution.
The "moment of truth" where actual client employees use the tool. If they don't "accept" it, the project isn't done, regardless of how good the code is.
Everything that happens after the FDE leaves. Includes monitoring, retraining models, and training the client's internal "Run Team".

resources.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
resources.note: (Martin Kleppmann): The "Bible". If you only read one book on this list, make it this one. It explains the why behind every database and distributed system you will use on GCP.

resources.title: The Trusted Advisor
resources.note: (David Maister): FDEs fail more often due to broken trust than broken code. This book teaches you how to move from a "vendor" to a "strategic partner".

resources.title: The Pyramid Principle
resources.note: (Barbara Minto): The McKinsey standard for communication. Learn to lead with the conclusion and support it with data—essential for talking to client executives.

resources.title: Enterprise Integration Patterns
resources.note: (Gregor Hohpe): Essential for Phase 2. It teaches you how to "glue" legacy systems together using messaging, gateways, and translators.

resources.title: Staff Engineer: Leadership beyond the management track
resources.note: (Will Larson): FDE is often a "Staff-plus" role in terms of scope. This book helps you navigate the high-level technical leadership required at client sites.

resources.title: The Google File System (2003)
resources.note: : The ancestor of GCS (Google Cloud Storage).

resources.title: Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (2006)
resources.note: : The foundation of NoSQL on GCP.

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need (2017)
resources.note: : The paper that started the Transformer/LLM revolution.

resources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (2023)
resources.note: : The logic behind how Agentic systems (like Google ADK) actually work.

resources.title: Latent Space
resources.note: : The best podcast for the "AI Engineer" era. Deep dives into RAG, Agents, and Evals.

resources.title: The Cognitive Revolution
resources.note: : Interviews with the people actually building the frontier models you will be deploying.

resources.title: Software Engineering Daily
resources.note: : Search their archives for "GCP," "Palantir," or "Distributed Systems".

resources.title: The Data Engineering Podcast
resources.note: : Vital for staying updated on the "Modern Data Stack".

resources.title: Import AI (Jack Clark)
resources.note: : A weekly summary of AI progress and—crucially—AI policy/safety.

resources.title: GCP Weekly
resources.note: : A non-official but highly curated list of every update in the Google Cloud ecosystem.

resources.title: Interconnects (Nathan Lambert)
resources.note: : Deep technical analysis of LLM training and alignment.

resources.title: The Pragmatic Engineer
resources.note: : Insights into how big tech companies actually operate and ship software.

resources.title: The AI Engineer (Paolo Perrone)
resources.note: : Weekly deep dives on production LLM inference: model selection, cost and latency tradeoffs, and the serving failure modes that surface when a demo meets a client's hardware.

resources.title: The Morning Paper (Archive)
resources.note: : A fantastic archive of CS paper summaries.

resources.title: Eugene Yan’s Blog
resources.note: : Incredible deep dives on building production-grade ML and Recommendation systems.

checklist.detail: Who is the internal person fighting for this project?
Which department (usually IT or Legal) is most likely to stop us?
Is success "Lower Latency," "Higher Accuracy," or "Headcount Reduction"?
Is the data PII, PHI, or Secret?
Do we need VPC Service Controls or Data Loss Prevention (DLP) masking?
Do we have Project Editor or Owner roles in the Google Cloud Project?
Is this a Private GKE cluster? Do we need a Cloud VPN or Interconnect?
Does the client have enough GPU quota (A100/H100) for the models we plan to deploy?
